mustKnow: Cholesterol builds up in an artery wall; the lumen narrows; a clot forms and blocks it
Less blood, so less oxygen and glucose reach the cells; less respiration; the cells die

Angioplasty widens a narrowed artery with a balloon; a stent holds it open
Statins lower blood cholesterol; aspirin makes platelets less sticky, so clots are less likely
Risk raised by too much dietary fat, smoking (stickier platelets), stress (blood pressure) and lack of exercise
Percentage change = change ÷ starting value × 100; a percentage of a total = total ÷ 100 × percentage

workedExamples.stem:
A trial compared two combinations of drugs for high blood pressure. The target was an average blood pressure below 140 arbitrary units.
(i) Calculate how many people in group 2 reached the target, to the nearest whole number. [3]
(ii) Give one piece of evidence from the table that drugs P and Q worked better. [1]

data.caption: A trial of two combinations of blood-pressure drugs
columns: Average blood pressure at the end / arbitrary units

steps.decision: A percentage is a number out of 100, so divide by 100 first.

options: Because a percentage means a number out of every 100
Because there are 100 people in each group
Because the answer must be less than 100
whyMenu.explain: 76.4% means 76.4 out of every 100, so 0.764 of the group. The groups here hold thousands of people.

steps.decision: Multiply by the whole group, the people in group 2.
Round to the nearest whole number, as asked: 3323.4 becomes 3323.

steps.working: 79.0% of group 1 reached the target, against 76.4% of group 2.
steps.decision: Compare percentages, not numbers of people: the groups are different sizes. (Group 1's lower average, 128.4 against 129.1, would also do.)

workedExamples.finalAnswer: (i) 3323 people. (ii) A higher percentage of group 1 reached the target: 79.0% against 76.4%.

items.stem: Before we start, three things from earlier topics. What do cells use glucose and oxygen for?

options.feedback: Respiration: glucose and oxygen release the energy a cell needs. Without them, a cell dies.
Photosynthesis makes glucose in plants. Cells use glucose and oxygen in respiration.
Digestion breaks food down. Cells use glucose and oxygen in respiration.
Cells use glucose and oxygen in respiration, to release energy.

items.stem: Which part of the blood helps it to clot?

options.feedback: Platelets: they stick together to form a clot. Aspirin makes them less sticky.
Red blood cells carry oxygen. Platelets help the blood clot.
White blood cells defend the body. Platelets help the blood clot.
Plasma carries dissolved substances. Platelets help the blood clot.

options.text: carry blood away from the heart
options.feedback: Arteries carry blood away from the heart, to the organs, and to the heart muscle itself.

options.text: carry blood back to the heart
options.feedback: That is what veins do. Arteries carry blood away from the heart.
That happens in capillaries. Arteries carry blood away from the heart.
No vessel stores blood. Arteries carry blood away from the heart.

items.stem: Which of these describes a heart attack?

options.text: heart muscle cells die because a coronary artery is blocked
options.feedback: Right: the cells beyond the blockage die. The heart often keeps beating.

options.text: the heart stops because a valve closes
options.feedback: A heart attack is heart muscle cells dying when a coronary artery is blocked, not the heart stopping.

options.text: brain cells die because an artery to the brain is blocked
options.feedback: That is a stroke. A heart attack is heart muscle cells dying.
A heart attack comes from an artery blocked, not widened.

items.stem: A clot blocks an artery that supplies the brain. What is the result called?

options.feedback: A stroke: brain cells die, and the brain works less well.
A heart attack is in the heart. In the brain, it is a stroke.
Emphysema is damage to the alveoli. In the brain, it is a stroke.
Diabetes is about blood glucose control. A blocked artery to the brain causes a stroke.

items.stem: Mr Kerr's blood cholesterol is very high. Which drug is prescribed to lower it?
items.skill: Choose the drug that lowers cholesterol

options.feedback: Statins lower the cholesterol in the blood, so less builds up in the arteries.
Aspirin makes platelets less sticky; it does not lower cholesterol. Statins do.
Antibiotics kill bacteria. The drug that lowers cholesterol is statins.
Insulin lowers blood glucose, not cholesterol. Statins lower cholesterol.

items.stem: A scan shows that a patient's coronary artery is already badly narrowed. Which treatment widens it straight away?
items.skill: Choose the treatment that reopens an artery

options.feedback: Angioplasty widens the narrowed part at once, and the stent holds it open.
Statins lower cholesterol over months, so less builds up; they do not reopen an artery already narrowed.
Aspirin makes a clot less likely; it does not widen the artery.
Stopping smoking lowers the risk of a clot, but it does not widen an artery that is already narrowed.

items.stem: Which change to a person's way of life lowers the risk of a heart attack by lowering the cholesterol in their blood?
items.skill: Link a fatty diet to cholesterol

options.feedback: Less fat in the diet means less cholesterol to build up in the arteries.
Stopping smoking helps, but through the platelets: they become less sticky. Less fat is what lowers cholesterol.
Lowering stress helps through blood pressure. Less fat is what lowers cholesterol.
Aspirin is a drug, not a change to a way of life, and it acts on the platelets, not on cholesterol.

parts.workedSolution: His narrowed artery can be treated by angioplasty: a small balloon is passed into the narrow part and inflated to widen it. A stent, a mesh tube, is then left inside to hold the artery open, so more blood, with its oxygen and glucose, reaches his heart muscle. Statins lower the cholesterol in his blood, so less builds up in his arteries and they are less likely to narrow again or become blocked. Aspirin makes his platelets less sticky, so a clot is less likely to form and block a coronary artery. He should also stop smoking: smoking makes platelets stickier, so stopping makes a clot less likely.

findTheMistake.stem:
Aoife is asked: 'A GP practice has 31,846 patients, and 28% of them take a statin every day. Calculate how many patients take a statin, correct to the nearest whole number. [3]'
Her working:
studentWorking: the total is 31846, and the part I want is 28% of it
findTheMistake.whatWentWrong: Line 2 divides by 28 and multiplies by 100, the slip the Summer 2025 examiners saw. The answer, 113735.7, is more patients than the whole practice has, which a part cannot be. To find 28% of the total, divide by 100 and multiply by 28.
correction: the total is 31846, and the part I want is 28% of it
findTheMistake.feedback: Line 1 reads the question well: the 31,846 is the whole. Then 1% is 31,846 ÷ 100 = 318.5, and 28% is 318.5 × 28 = 8916.9, so 8,917 patients. Check: it is smaller than the total.

findTheMistake.stem:
Conor is asked: 'In a trial, the average cholesterol of a group taking statins fell from 7.5 to 5.1 arbitrary units. Calculate the percentage fall. [2]'
His working:
findTheMistake.whatWentWrong: Line 2 divides by 5.1, the value at the end. A percentage fall is always a share of where it started, 7.5, so divide by that.
findTheMistake.feedback: The fall in line 1 is right, 2.4. Divide it by the starting value: 2.4 ÷ 7.5 × 100 = 32%.
